lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Multi-Digit Multiplication with Area Models and Partial Products
lessonRef.title: Concept extension: multiplicative comparison with larger numbers

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example applies the idea in a new setting. Notice what stayed the same.

items.prompt: Sam read 4 books. Priya read 5 times as many as Sam. How many did Priya read?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what is different about this case before you start.

items.prompt: Carlos read 11 books this year. Emma read 3 times as many books as Carlos. How many books did Emma read?
Carlos read 10 books this year. Emma read 4 times as many books as Carlos. How many books did Emma read?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Ben read 8 books this year. Priya read 2 times as many books as Ben. How many books did Priya read?
Ben read 7 books this year. Priya read 2 times as many books as Ben. How many books did Priya read?
Ben read 11 books this year. Priya read 3 times as many books as Ben. How many books did Priya read?
Ben read 12 books this year. Priya read 6 times as many books as Ben. How many books did Priya read?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain, in writing, what made this case different from the original one.

items.prompt: Ben read 9 books this year. Priya read 3 times as many books as Ben. How many books did Priya read?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Ben read 2 books this year. Priya read 4 times as many books as Ben. How many books did Priya read?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
